[[Category:Organisation&efficiency]]
[[File:Metra-Potential-Method-MPM-Example.svg|thumbnail|An example graphical representation of MPM]]
First developped by Bernard Roy et al.,<ref>{{#cite:Q3286}}</ref> '''Metra Potential Method (MPM)''' is a method for organising different '''tasks''' ($J_j$) in a [[scheduling problem]] by

* analysing the dependency of each tasks ($J_{jx},J_{jy} \dots \to J_{jz}$)
* Identify thereby the theoretical earliest start time for each task ($t_i(j)$)
* Identify the final due time ($T^*$)
* Calculate backwards the latest start time for each task for respecting the due time ($t^*_i(j)$).

== Slack ==

'''Slack''' is additional time available (for unexpected delays, etc.) without impacting performance on specific criteria.

=== Total slack ===

$$
\text{Total slack}=t^*_i(j)-t^_i(j)
$$

which measures the available slack for task $J_j$ without impacting overall finish time, '''given there is no other delay elsewhere'''.

=== Free slack ===

$$
\text{Free slack}=t_i(j+1)-t_f(j)
$$

which measures the available slack for task $J_j$ without impacting the start time of tasks that depend on it.

In general,

$$
\text{Free slack} \le \text{Total slack}
$$
